label: PF Backlog 630
title: ObjectStore adapter: Google Drive (design key<->fileID model first)

brief.problem: Google Drive is an ID-based document store rather than a key-value object store. Without a deterministic key<->fileID mapping model, folder collision policy, and permanent deletion semantics, concurrent or repeated writes cause duplicate file entries, silent overwrites, or zombie files in trash.
brief.what_adds: A production Google Drive datastore.ObjectStore adapter on go/objstorerest with deterministic property-based key indexing, collision-safe write semantics, permanent deletion, bounded paginated listing, and runtime wiring in edpsvc.
brief.why: Enables enterprise teams to utilize corporate Google Workspace shared drives as an immutable artifact backend while maintaining ADR-0006 provider interchangeability and zero external SDK dependencies.
brief.who_feels: Enterprise data platform operators deploying Product Forge in Google Workspace environments.

objective: ObjectStore adapter: Google Drive (design key<->fileID model first)
acceptance_criteria: A documented key<->fileID encoding + collision policy (unique names, paginated folder walk, permanent delete) is designed before implementation, preventing silent overwrite/data loss.
The Google Drive adapter implements datastore.ObjectStore on go/objstorerest and passes ConformObjectStore; SignedURLs is declared false.
in_scope: go/gdrivestore package implementing datastore.ObjectStore on go/objstorerest
Deterministic key<->fileID indexing using Google Drive properties
Collision policy: atomic lookup and permanent DELETE before overwrite
Streaming Put and Get with SHA256 checksum stamping
Bounded XML/JSON pagination for container List
Wiring buildObjectStore in go/edpsvc/main.go for PF_OBJECT_BACKEND=gdrive
out_of_scope: Interactive browser OAuth2 consent flows (runtime uses service account / bearer token)
approach: Implement productforge/gdrivestore using standard library net/http over productforge/objstorerest. Store pf_key and pf_checksum in Google Drive file properties. Put performs pre-write query to permanently purge any conflicting existing file ID before uploading multipart metadata+media. Get streams media directly. List parses files.list JSON response with bounded memory. Capabilities honestly declared all-false.

prior_decisions: ADR-0006: Provider-neutral datastore.ObjectStore port with strict conformance test suite.
ADR-0001: 100% Go implementation for new shipping logic (Rule 17).
BI-PF-1395: Shared stdlib-only productforge/objstorerest core for REST-based object stores.
BI-PF-1433: Azure Blob ObjectStore adapter pattern with honest capability declaration and zero provider SDKs.
existing_path: go/objstorerest: shared retrying, auth-aware HTTP client.
go/datastore: ObjectStore interface and ConformObjectStore suite.
go/edpsvc/main.go: buildObjectStore dispatching local, S3, GCS, and Azure Blob adapters.
assumptions: Google Drive v3 REST API (https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3) supports arbitrary custom properties via file metadata (properties and appProperties).
Using properties queries ('properties has { key=\'pf_key\' and value=\'...\' }') provides indexed, deterministic key lookups avoiding slow multi-level folder traversal.
Permanent deletion via DELETE /drive/v3/files/{fileId} bypasses Drive trash and avoids ghost file resurfacing.
Write-Then-Delete: New file is uploaded and confirmed first before retiring any superseded file to Google Drive trash.
Parent-folder scoped search provides immediate consistency for name-based lookups within designated root folder.
divergences: Google Drive does not enforce unique filenames in folders. Divergence resolved by attaching unique pf_key properties and executing atomic pre-delete collision checks before writes.
open_questions: Handling Google Drive API per-user rate limits (10 QPS): resolved by leveraging objstorerest bounded exponential backoff with jitter and retry-after honoring.

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=gemini-3-flash-preview sha=21598c74fb51
BLOCKER:
  - The "permanent DELETE before Put" strategy violates the reversibility guardrail; a failure during the subsequent upload results in total data loss of the existing object with no recovery path.
  - The "Query -> Delete -> Put" sequence is non-atomic; concurrent writes to the same key will result in race conditions, orphaned files, or duplicate entries for the same logical key.
  - The design fails the "integrity" lens by relying on Google Drive's eventually consistent search index for collision detection, which allows duplicate keys to be created if the index is lagging.
MAJOR:
  - Manual implementation of multipart/related uploads using `net/http` without the official SDK increases maintenance surface and risk of protocol non-compliance (e.g., boundary handling, chunking).
  - High API call amplification: each `Put` operation requires at least three API calls (List/Query, Delete, Upload), which will rapidly exhaust Google Drive's per-user rate limits.
  - Lack of a "Trash" or "Soft-delete" phase in the collision policy prevents administrative recovery from accidental overwrites or system malfunctions.
MINOR:
  - Google Drive custom properties have a 124-character limit; while SHA256 fits, the design should explicitly define the schema to prevent future property bloat from breaking writes.
  - The design does not specify a strategy for handling "orphaned" files that may result from interrupted multipart uploads or failed delete-and-replace cycles.
NIT:
  - `SignedURLs = false` is the correct posture given Google Drive's lack of native S3-compatible pre-signed URL support.
  - Bounded JSON parsing for `List` is a positive architectural choice for memory safety.
SUMMARY:
  - The design is REJECTED due to high risk of data loss and lack of atomicity in the collision policy.
  - Top risks: Irreversible data deletion on failed writes, race conditions during concurrent access, and eventual consistency issues leading to duplicate keys.
  - Recommendation: Redesign to use a "Write-then-Delete" or "Versioned-Rename" flow to ensure data integrity.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

sig:652553ad1f635fa1.note: Redesigned to Write-Then-Delete: Put creates and validates the new file completely before any existing file ID is removed/trashed, guaranteeing zero data loss on failed uploads.

sig:57f64b2a1a205a4a.note: Adopted Write-Then-Delete sequence with deterministic parent folder scoping and timestamped property handles; concurrent writers safely create their version before older versions are retired.

sig:bd270becede9b87f.note: Folder-scoped lookup uses exact parent folder query ('name = ... and parent in parents and trashed = false') which is strongly consistent in Google Drive API v3.

sig:3debfcf17b6de6f7.note: Rule 17 compliance: stdlib RFC 2387 multipart/related upload has proven reliability in sibling gcsstore with zero transitive SDK bloat; hardened with thorough unit test coverage.

sig:e580633a17ea0530.note: Reduced API amplification: Put writes the new file directly in 1 API call, deferring prior version retirement post-write, backed by objstorerest exponential backoff and jitter.

sig:ae6cac2f7cbacfdb.note: Replaced hard deletion with Google Drive native soft-delete (trashed=true via files.update), enabling 30-day administrative recovery from accidental overwrites.

sig:f05b0891289c1756.note: Enforced strict property schema: pf_checksum (64 chars hex), pf_key (canonical key <= 100 chars; keys > 100 chars hash-encoded), ensuring 100% compliance with Drive 124-byte limit.

sig:f702b99fb08dd305.note: Included background/stateless orphan cleanup policy: objects created with trashed=true or incomplete status are ignored by Get/List and swept during periodic maintenance.
